title: The martyrs of Libya (15 February)
hookLine: Coptic Christians killed on a beach in Libya, now honored in the Roman Martyrology

cards: Today's saints were not from long ago. They were workers, in our own time: men who had left their villages in Egypt to find jobs in Libya and send money home to their families.
They were kidnapped by an armed group, dressed in orange, led onto a beach by the sea, and killed. Their killers filmed it and sent the film around the world.
Reports of the film say that, at the end, some of the men were heard calling on Jesus. The Church remembers them as the martyrs of Libya.

teach.b: Almost all the men were Coptic Orthodox Christians, from the ancient Church of Egypt. One who died with them was from Ghana, and tradition among the Copts holds that he chose to stand with the others.
Here's what makes this day unusual in a Catholic calendar.

teach.h: A CHURCH NOT IN FULL COMMUNION WITH ROME.
teach.b: The Coptic Orthodox Church is not in full communion with Rome. It has its own pope in Alexandria, its own liturgy, its own saints. Their pope declared these men martyrs and saints of his Church.
Later, Pope Francis received the Coptic pope at the Vatican and announced that the men would be added to the Roman Martyrology, the Catholic Church's official list of saints and martyrs.
A Church honoring martyrs who were not its own members, because of how they died.

Pope Francis had a phrase for this: an ecumenism of blood. Those who kill Christians, he said in effect, don't stop to ask which church they belong to. Catholics and Copts still differ on real questions, and both say so.
But in the Martyrology, the names stand together. In the Greek of the Acts of the Apostles, the word for witnesses is the word English borrowed as martyr.

teach.h: YOU SHALL BE WITNESSES UNTO ME.
teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims, Jesus tells his followers, "you shall be witnesses unto me," and sends that witness to the uttermost part of the earth. A beach in Libya is one of those far places. These men preached no sermon there.
Their witness was a name on their lips.

how: The Coptic Orthodox Church keeps these men as martyrs and saints on 15 February, and since their inclusion in the Roman Martyrology Catholics also remember them that day, often praying for Christians who suffer for their faith.

practice: Bring to mind the families in those villages who sent their sons out to work and waited for calls that stopped coming, then widen it to Coptic Christians today, in Egypt and in cities all over the world, getting up for church, raising children, burying their dead.
If you pray, hold them before God in your own words or with the Lord's Prayer; if you don't, give one breath to the families and one to the men.

wordCard.voice: Ecumenism. Pope Francis's word for what unites Catholics and Copts killed for Christ: the Coptic Christians of this day, killed on a Libyan beach, declared saints by their own Church and added to the Catholic Martyrology.

orig.note: Greek: a witness. the word behind martyr, and behind "witnesses" in the Acts of the Apostles.

carryVoice: Your line: the twenty-one. Different churches, and their names stand on one list. Day nine hundred sixty-eight.
